title: ECC scrub & eviction workflow notes (draft)
content:
Purpose: quick, pragmatic runbook draft for handling nodes showing repeated soft ECC bursts, escalating NVLink packet drops, or frequent driver crashes that correlate with memory-scrub remediation. This is intentionally operational — prioritize safe isolation and customer impact reduction over deep root-cause analysis.

Scope: applies to GPU tenant nodes in our Dedicated and Private fleets where ECC errors or periodic kernel-driver faults have been observed. Not a full postmortem — this is a field guide for on-call engineers and SREs to standardize actions and telemetry checks.

High-level goals:
- Detect when soft ECC errors are recurring enough to justify proactive eviction.
- Execute safe eviction that minimizes lost in-flight requests and preserves KV cache integrity where possible.
- Capture a consistent set of logs and artifacts to accelerate follow-up RCA.
- Provide fallback routing rules and prioritized remediation steps (scrub, firmware update, replacement).

Key signals to consider (first-line telemetry):
- ECC corrected error rate above baseline: > 50 corrected errors per GPU in 10m OR error rate spike > 10x baseline. Query: metric gpu_ecc_corrected_total by instance, increase over 10m.
- NVLink retransmit/packet-drop metric > 0.5% per link averaged across link partners for > 5m.
- Driver crashes / dmesg OOPS containing nvidia/uctld/tesla stack traces within past 30m.
- CUDA context loss metrics: context_loss_count > 0 with client-request failure rate rising by >3%.
- Memory scrubbing triggers causing sustained device stall > 200ms or repeated IRQs.

Immediate on-call checklist (ordered):
1) Triage & communicate (0–5m):
   - Announce incident in #sre-gpu with short summary: node, fleet, signal (ECC spike / NVLink drops / driver crash), impact (affected clusters/tenants).
   - If customer impact detected, page CS/Support per escalation matrix.

2) Quick telemetry snapshot (5–10m):
   - Run: journalctl -u nvidia-driver -S "-30m" | tail -n 200; dmesg | tail -n 200
   - Query Prometheus: increase(gpu_ecc_corrected_total[10m]) by instance; rate(nvlink_packet_drop_total[5m]) / rate(nvlink_packet_sent_total[5m]) per link.
   - Check GPU health endpoint: curl -s http://host:9100/metrics | grep -E "gpu_ecc_corrected|nvlink_packet_drop|cuda_context_loss"

3) Apply soft mitigations (10–20m):
   - If ECC spike only and no driver crash: mark node for immediate background ECC scrub via firmware/driver path if supported (see vendor doc snippet in linked artifacts). Schedule scrub window and set node to cordon-like state for new allocations if workload tolerance is low.
   - If NVLink drops or driver instability present: proactively drain long-running jobs (best-effort) and prevent new assignments. Use graceful eviction script: /opt/redwood/bin/gpu-evict --host <host> --mode graceful --timeout 300s.

4) Eviction decision matrix (20–30m):
   - Condition A (low customer impact, single GPU, corrected ECC counts slowly rising): schedule scrub and keep node in soft-cordon. Recheck 2h after scrub.
   - Condition B (multiple GPUs affected, NVLink errors, or driver crashes seen): immediate hard-drain and remove from rotation pending hardware swap or firmware downgrade. Raise change request for replacement.
   - Condition C (driver kernel panic or repeated CUDA context loss causing client errors): hard-drain, attach debug snapshot, and escalate to hardware ops and applied-ml for possible model checkpoint rehydration guidance.

5) Artifact collection (during or immediately after eviction):
   - Collect: /var/log/nvidia-installer.log, journalctl -u nvidia-driver -S "-2h" > driver-journal.txt, sudo /usr/bin/nvtop -b 1 > nvtop-snapshot.txt, /proc/driver/nvidia/gpus/*/error_stats (copy), and smartctl output for host disks.
   - Export vendor diag tools: nvdiag --collect --outfile /tmp/nvdiag-<host>-<ts>.tar.gz
   - Upload artifacts to S3 incident bucket: rclone copy /tmp/nvdiag-*.tar.gz s3:sre-incidents/2026-01-<host>/

6) Temporary routing fallback (if customers affected):
   - Promote hot-standby nodes or route affected tenant traffic to lower-capacity pool with throttling. Use routing rule: route_policy=evict_fallback in routing service. Ensure keys for customer pinned sessions are honored or resumed if possible.

Post-eviction validation (30–60m):
- Confirm all in-flight requests gracefully failed-over or resumed. Check application error metrics for spike or leakage.
- Re-check GPU metrics for continued ECC bursts; if repeat within 4h mark for mandatory replacement.
- If scrub completed: re-run correctness tests (model smoke tests) and run 15m of increased monitoring before rejoining.

Suggested escalation paths and owners:
- Hardware swap & firmware: hw-ops@redwood with ticket SRE-4821 assigned to Marcus Lee.
- Driver/kernel correlation RCA: eng-kernel-team and infra-release-owner Jenna Ortiz.
- Model/ML impact: applied-ml oncall (Kai Müller).

Open questions needing follow-up (RCA backlog items):
- Do scrubs at scale introduce transient latency that meaningfully impacts dedicated tenants? Need controlled experiment during low traffic.
- Can we detect NVLink soft-failure earlier by combining PCIe error trends and link-flap deltas? Build a composite signal and test for 2 weeks.
- Evaluate whether a rolling firmware downgrade path should be part of automated remediation for driver-induced memory-scrub storms.

Metrics & dashboard recommendations (quick list):
- Live chart: gpu_ecc_corrected_rate per GPU and 10m rolling avg, with alert when >50 errs/10m.
- Link-level NVLink drop ratio with 5m rate and alert for >0.5%.
- Driver crash trend: count of driver-reload events per host per hour.
- Eviction impact panel: number of drained hosts, reassign rate, tenant error rate.

Runbook caveats and safety notes:
- Never reboot a host in the middle of a long-running checkpointing job without coordinating with tenant owners if possible. Prefer graceful eviction.
- Some GPUs will clear corrected ECC counts after a scrub and appear healthy; repeated scrubs (more than 3 within 7d) is a replacement signal.
- Avoid in-place firmware upgrades during business hours; schedule as part of maintenance windows unless emergency.

Action items (owners and due dates):
- (Aisha) Implement graceful eviction wrapper script improvements: add --preserve-kv-cache flag and dry-run mode. Due 2026-02-05.
- (Marcus) Create vendor diagnostic playbook with exact scrub commands for our fleet variants. Due 2026-02-12.
- (Jenna) Add composite NVLink signal to alerting and run 2-week trial. Due 2026-02-28.

Appendix: quick commands for on-call
- Check ECC counts: prometheus_query "increase(gpu_ecc_corrected_total[10m]) by (instance)"
- NVLink drop ratio: prometheus_query "rate(nvlink_packet_drop_total[5m]) / rate(nvlink_packet_sent_total[5m])"
- Trigger graceful eviction: /opt/redwood/bin/gpu-evict --host gpu-node-23 --mode graceful --timeout 300s
- Collect driver journal: journalctl -u nvidia-driver -S "-2h" > /tmp/driver-journal.txt

Notes-to-self: keep this doc short and operational, move technical deep-dive (firmware quirks, vendor-specific scrubs) into vendor playbook linked above. Intend to iterate after next two evictions to tune thresholds.

If you're reading this during oncall: prefer communication over perfection — get node out of rotation, capture artifacts, then worry about root cause.
